Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Subject: Close orchestration: MAP & legal dependencies for VitalCore pilot

Hannah / Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency profile. We want to lock the pilot timeline with clear checkpoints so procurement and security can align to your MSA/DPA/order form sequencing. A few constraints on our side:
- Procurement needs an executed order form + PO by 11/19 to hit the December budget window.
- Security wants confirmation of DPA terms (data residency and subprocessors) before infra access.
- Our legal will push redlines to the MSA if we see non-standard indemnities.

Can you send a mutual action plan that maps: evaluation milestones -> legal review windows -> order form execution? Also please include who from Redwood will own DPA redlines and the expected review SLA. I attached our risk register for background.

If we can agree on a 3-week MAP with gated approvals, procurement can commit to the PO timeline. Proposed kickoff: 11/10 (technical onboarding) if legal gating is resolved.

Thanks,
Sandeep Rao
Head of Platform Integrations
VitalCore Health
[sent from mobile]

Subject: Re: Close orchestration: MAP & legal dependencies for VitalCore pilot

Sandeep —

Great context, thanks. Draft MAP attached (Redwood_MAP_template_v1.xlsx). High-level plan I propose:
1) 11/03–11/05: Redwood legal & VitalCore legal exchange initial redlines (MSA/DPA).
2) 11/06–11/12: Technical eval + security evidence collection (SOC2 snippets, data flow diagram).
3) 11/13–11/17: Procurement reviews order form + PO issuance window.
4) 11/19: Target order form signature / PO submission.

Key owners: Jordan will own order form/pricing confirmations; Karthik (cc'd) will lead MSA/DPA redline coordination. I asked Legal to do an expedited review with a 48-hour SLA on redline responses where possible. If VitalCore can accept the standard Redwood DPA sections except for subprocessors, we can shorten the legal window by a week.

Next steps: 1) Karthik will send a short redline playbook + acceptable fallback positions, 2) Jordan will share a one-page order summary for procurement by EOD tomorrow, 3) Sandeep / Maya to confirm procurement lead and PO date.

Open asks for you: who at VitalCore will sign (procurement or VP of Ops)? and any non-standard terms we should expect up front?

Hannah Schmitt
Director, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: MSA / DPA redline path and acceptance gates

Team / Sandeep —

Quick legal playbook so procurement has clarity:
- We reviewed VitalCore_Risk_Register and there are two items that could expand DPA negotiation time: subprocessors list and export controls clause. If VitalCore can accept Redwood's standard subprocessors list for the pilot scope, we can keep negotiation to 48–72 hours.
- Attached are annotated MSA redlines (MSA_redlines_20261103.docx). These highlight only three substantive changes we will push on (IP carveouts, liability cap alignment, and audit rights language). Everything else is commentary.
- Proposed acceptance gates for a fast path: 1) VitalCore accepts standard DPA (or sends modifications limited to Appendix A) by 11/09, 2) Procurement confirms PO intent by 11/12, 3) Order form signed by 11/19. If gate 1 slips, target start moves to 12/06.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/secure/embeddedSigning?doc=VC-4839-orderform
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4839

If you want we can run a 2-week gated sprint (11/10–11/24) that keeps technical onboarding scoped to a sandbox until legal closes. That minimizes risk and doesn't block engineering ramp.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: MSA_redlines_20261103.docx (Word doc)
